title: Extension of generic homomorphisms of semiabelian schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral locally Noetherian scheme and let $P,Q\to S$ be semiabelian schemes (smooth separated commutative groups of finite presentation with semiabelian geometric fibres). Every homomorphism $P_\eta\to Q_\eta$ of generic fibres extends uniquely to a homomorphism $P\to Q$ over $S$. [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-integral-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth] [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres]

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1.5, citing Faltings–Chai I, Proposition 2.7 and Raynaud IX 1.4.

proof.text: For $n=1,2$, apply [lem-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-power-integrality] to each algebraically closed geometric fibre of $P$: its $n$th power is integral, hence connected and nonempty. By [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-algebraic-closure], the fibres of $P$ and $P\times_SP$ are geometrically connected. The latter is smooth: its first projection is the base change of $P\to S$ by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), and compose using [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. Apply [lem-sbc-smooth-connected-generic-geometry-core] to both families. Thus $P$, $P\times_SP$ and their generic fibres are integral with integrally closed local rings. The identity sections make both families surjective. Consequently their generic points lie over $\eta$: the image of a generic point specializes to every point of the surjective image, and an integral scheme has only one generic point. Moreover $P$ is locally Noetherian. Indeed over any Noetherian affine open of $S$, it is finite type since it is of finite presentation; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes this inverse image Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 034F, lemma-normal-local-smooth; assembly from the cited geometric-integrality and Noetherian-ascent statements.

proof.text: Let $u:P_\eta\to Q_\eta$ be the prescribed homomorphism and form its scheme-theoretic graph closure $\Gamma$ in $P\times_SQ$, with first projection $\pi:\Gamma\to P$, as in [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. Apply [lem-sfb-semiabelian-generic-graph-proper] and [lem-sfb-semiabelian-generic-graph-finite-fibres] to these same $S,P,Q,u$. They give properness of $\pi$ and finite underlying sets for every fibre. Since $P$ is locally Noetherian by step 1, [thm-pqf-finite-iff-proper-finite-fibres] implies that $\pi$ is finite.

source.place: G. Faltings, Finiteness Theorems for Abelian Varieties over Number Fields, in Arithmetic Geometry (1986), Chapter II, section 2, Lemma 1 proof, printed pp.10-11: the two assertions about the projection of the graph closure. Local copy WANTED; online primary-source proof read at https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~lefourns/contenu/Zywina/Faltings.pdf .

proof.text: The graph inclusion $a:P_\eta\to P\times_SQ$ factors through $\Gamma$ by the defining universal property of its scheme-theoretic image. Its first projection is the canonical map $P_\eta\to P$. Let $\xi$ be the generic point of the integral scheme $P$. It lies in $P_\eta$ by step 1. Restrict $a$ to $\operatorname{Spec}k(P)$ to get a prescribed generic section of the finite map $\pi$. The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-finite-normal-generic-section-extension] hold: its base is now $P$, which is integral and normal by step 1, and its finite source is $\Gamma$, on which that lemma requires no normality or reducedness. It supplies a section $s:P\to\Gamma$ extending this generic section. Define $f:P\to Q$ to be $s$ followed by the second projection. Thus $f$ is an $S$-morphism agreeing with $u$ at the generic point $\xi$ of $P_\eta$.

source.place: Tag 0AB1, lemma-finite-birational-over-normal; the already existing finite generic-section extension formulation.

proof.text: Use the following elementary equality test. Two $S$-maps from an integral scheme $X$ to the separated $S$-scheme $Q$ that agree on $\operatorname{Spec}k(X)$ are equal: their equalizer is the pullback of the closed diagonal; on every nonempty affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$ its ideal $I\subset A$ maps to zero in $\operatorname{Frac}A$, so $I=0$ since $A$ is a domain. Apply this first to $f|_{P_\eta}$ and $u$ on the integral generic fibre; step 3 gives equality at its generic point, so $f|_{P_\eta}=u$. Next apply the same test to the two maps $f\circ m_P$ and $m_Q\circ(f\times f)$ from the integral $P\times_SP$. Its generic point lies over $\eta$, and the maps agree there because $u$ is a group homomorphism. Apply it on $S$ to $f\circ e_P$ and $e_Q$ as well. Hence $f$ preserves addition and the identity, and inverses follow from these two identities by the group axioms. Finally, any second $S$-group homomorphism extending $u$ agrees with $f$ at $\xi$; the same test on $P$ proves equality. This proves both existence and uniqueness.
